description: Pilot capsule for the pure orchestration-ask timeout clamp policy: no Electron, DOM, filesystem, network, or process dependency in the pinned files.
sourceRevisionNote: Verified via `git -C <source-root> rev-parse HEAD` at manifest authoring time; the runner re-verifies this on every invocation and refuses to stage on any mismatch.
dependencyClosureNote: orchestration-ask-timeout.test.ts imports only ./orchestration-ask-timeout and ./timer-delay (both relative, no aliasing). timer-delay.ts has zero imports. This is the complete transitive closure; no other legacy source file is read, staged, or executed by this capsule.
sourceVitestConfigDifferencesFromCapsule: source test.environment is 'node' (matches capsule; no difference here)
source defines a global constant ORCA_FEATURE_WALL_ENABLED='true' at build time; the capsule's generated config defines nothing, since the pinned files never reference it

source registers three setupFiles (config/scripts/happy-dom-offscreen-canvas.ts, config/scripts/happy-dom-mutation-observer-retention.ts, config/scripts/vitest-host-ports-setup.ts); the capsule registers none, since the pinned files touch no DOM/canvas/host-port surface
source sets hookTimeout=60000ms and testTimeout=30000ms for its full, heavier suite; the capsule uses Vitest's built-in defaults

source passes execArgv ['--no-experimental-webstorage','--expose-gc'] to the worker process for retention tests elsewhere in the suite; the capsule passes none, since the pinned files allocate nothing that a GC-timing test would observe

installed capsule runner uses vitest 5.0.0 (apps/desktop/node_modules/.bin/vitest); the source project pins vitest ^4.1.11 in its own package.json. This is a real, unverified compatibility gap for anything beyond these two plain arithmetic/clamping assertions -- do not treat a pass under 5.0.0 as proof the source suite passes under its own pinned 4.1.11.
isolationRationale: Both pinned modules are side-effect-free, import-free-of-runtime (timer-delay.ts has zero imports; orchestration-ask-timeout.ts imports nothing), and export only pure numeric functions/constants. The test file imports only these two sibling modules by relative path. No Electron, IPC, filesystem, network, timer-scheduling, or global mutation occurs anywhere in this closure, which is why this capsule was approved to execute; this property does not generalize to other files in the source tree.
